answer.rationale: The write-path p99 degradation is confined to the primary region and has been climbing for 90 minutes, suggesting a region-local resource or infrastructure issue rather than a release-level defect. The release deployed 2 hours ago contains a compliance-mandated security patch that cannot be rolled back, eliminating rollback_release. At peak settlement traffic with heavy writes, we cannot afford to add capacity and wait for it to spin up while p99 continues to climb — the risk of losing customer writes increases every minute we delay. Regional failover (memory_b2, day 33) previously restored latency fast during a similar region-scoped degradation; traffic shifted cleanly and error rates recovered within minutes. This is the only candidate that (1) moves the write path off the degraded primary immediately, (2) preserves the mandatory security-patch release in the serving set, and (3) protects settlement writes by shifting them to a healthy region rather than absorbing them on the degraded primary. Routing to read replicas (memory_b5) addresses read-side dashboard load, not write-path latency. Enabling a circuit breaker (memory_b4) would shed settlement traffic, violating the objective of not losing customer writes. Adding capacity is slower to materialize relief and does not address a region-scoped degradation. I am requesting verification of memory_b2 to confirm the failover procedure and recovery-time details before committing, but the directional evidence from all six memories — particularly the region-scoped containment pattern in b2 and the staged-release discipline in b6 — strongly supports failover as the single highest-value intervention this window.
